stated: Labour will support the transition to electric vehicles by accelerating the rollout of charge points. They will restore the 2030 phase-out date for new internal combustion engine cars and support buyers of second-hand electric cars by standardising battery condition information.

source.quote: Labour will support the transition to electric vehicles by accelerating the roll out of charge points, giving certainty to manufacturers by restoring the phase-out date of 2030 for new cars with internal combustion engines, and supporting buyers of second-hand electric cars by standardising the information supplied on the condition of batteries.

bearing_set.reason: Restoring the 2030 ICE phase-out and accelerating charge-point rollout directly targets road-transport emissions trajectory and urban air quality — core O6 indicators.

The 2030 phase-out compels households to buy EVs (currently carrying a purchase-price premium over equivalent ICE cars), directly affecting real disposable income and the inflation basket for car-dependent households; the battery-condition standardisation measure specifically addresses the information-asymmetry cost risk in the second-hand EV market, confirming the policy itself recognises the affordability mechanism.

Setting a firm 2030 deadline creates regulatory certainty that shapes business investment in EV manufacturing, supply chains and infrastructure, with real near-term transition costs and long-term living-standards effects — a dual-horizon economic verdict on productivity and opportunity.

Restoring the 2030 ban on new ICE car sales is a state mandate that restricts what consumers can purchase in a major market, directly engaging the 'freedom from state coercion / mandates' indicator under O10.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: O6 (the policy's stated environmental purpose), O13 (economic transition effects on investment and living standards), and O10 (the coercive dimension of banning new ICE sales). A fourth candidate, O2 (transport running costs), was considered but the effect is indirect and contingent on adoption rates — it does not clear the non-negligible bar independently of O13.
